title: Towards Human-AI Deliberation: Design and Evaluation of LLM-Empowered Deliberative AI for AI-Assisted Decision-Making

bias_targets.methodology: Quantitative measurement of human over-reliance on AI using the 'Over-reliance Ratio' (the fraction of tasks where participants adopted an incorrect AI prediction) and 'Switch Fraction' (the percentage of tasks where users changed their initial decision to agree with the AI).

Qualitative analysis of participants' conversation logs and open-ended feedback to observe if the human-AI deliberation process helped users identify inherent social biases in the AI's reasoning, specifically instances where the AI favored U.S. applicants while downplaying those from Asia.

Evaluated conceptually by assessing whether the system's 'cognitive forcing' design (which requires users to form independent opinions before viewing AI recommendations) successfully counters the undue influence of initial AI predictions on human judgment.
